title: CRB-65
subtitle: Community-acquired pneumonia risk
summary: CRB-65 estimates mortality risk in adults with clinically suspected community-acquired pneumonia when blood urea is unavailable.
population: Adults with clinically suspected community-acquired pneumonia when blood urea is unavailable.

criteria.label: New confusion
criteria.description: New disorientation to person, place or time, or an AMTS of 8 or less where used.

criteria.label: Low blood pressure
criteria.description: Systolic below 90 mmHg or diastolic 60 mmHg or lower.

results.label: Low predicted mortality risk
interpretation: Home treatment may be suitable only if no other clinical or social concern exists.

results.label: Increased risk
interpretation: Consider hospital assessment, especially at score 2.

results.label: High risk
interpretation: Urgent hospital assessment is usually required.

overrides: Hypoxia, respiratory distress, inability to speak full sentences, cyanosis, new confusion, systolic BP below 90 mmHg, rapidly worsening symptoms, inability to maintain oral intake or major comorbidity can override a low score.
limitations: CRB-65 does not detect sepsis, pulmonary embolism, acute heart failure or inability to cope at home.

clinicalValidation.reviewNotes: Formal clinical verification has not yet been recorded. Population, exclusions, thresholds, calculations, wording and implementation tests must be checked against the cited source.
